headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: caveman can ingest files and use MCP, while dbt-core can act on warehouse data and send it to an allowlisted backend.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can read local files like CLAUDE.md and project notes and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content could reach its instruction context. dbt-core has no documented parsing of caveman output, but the pair still has a plausible shared-channel pathway via files/MCP. Uncertainty about the exact bridge keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman ingests untrusted file content through CLAUDE.md or project notes
IF an MCP server or shared file is used to pass caveman output into dbt-core workflows
mitigations: Restrict caveman to trusted prompt files only
Separate the two agents into different workspaces
Disable MCP for caveman during paired runs
Review any file passed from caveman before dbt-core consumes it
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress. If caveman content is forwarded into dbt-core, sensitive project data can cross into a networked analytics path. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF caveman outputs files containing session logs or project notes into a workspace dbt-core reads
IF dbt-core sends warehouse-derived context to its allowlisted backend
mitigations: Keep warehouse data out of caveman-managed files
Use separate service accounts and workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff
Audit allowlisted egress destinations for dbt-core
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filters at the workspace boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and can use MCP, but it has no filesystem write or network egress beyond none. dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse access, yet no overlapping write surface is documented. The pair shows limited conflict potential, mainly if an orchestrator lets both mutate the same shared resource.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same shared warehouse object
IF an external orchestrator grants both mutable access to one resource without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct resource scopes
Avoid concurrent writes to the same target
Serialize runs through one orchestrator queue
Check for overlapping warehouse permissions
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can produce project notes and CLAUDE.md content that dbt-core could consume as downstream input, and dbt-core can then act on warehouse data or emit transformed outputs. There is no documented verification step between them, so an error or hallucination from caveman can propagate into dbt-core workflows. The lack of direct evidence prevents high.
conditions: IF dbt-core uses caveman-generated notes or files as authoritative inputs
IF no human or automated validation occurs before dbt-core executes
mitigations: Require review before dbt-core runs
Compare caveman outputs against source data
Limit caveman to drafting only
Log provenance for every handoff
requires-engineering: add validation gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while dbt-core touches warehouse data. The profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so only a small compliance gap is evidenced. Because the relevant compliance fields are absent for both, the other agent is cited only to show the data-class context.
conditions: IF either agent stores regulated data in its touched files or warehouse tables
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before use
Avoid placing regulated data in caveman files
Confirm warehouse retention settings
Document deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
